title: semgate-check/1
description: One proposed tool call, for semgate.check() and POST /v1/check. semgate never runs the tool; it answers allow, ask or deny. Everything here is data from the caller's own records: user_messages must come from the caller's record of what the human typed, never from model output or tool results.

schema.description: Optional. When present it must be this value.

tool.description: Tool name. Known names and aliases (bash, shell, run_command, read, read_file, write, edit, glob, grep, ls, web_fetch, web_search, ...) map to semgate's canonical names (semgate.harness.TOOL_ALIASES); any other name is judged as given.

arguments.description: The tool's arguments as the model produced them. A shell tool puts its command line in `command`; a file tool its path in `path` (filePath / file_path are copied to path).

session_id.description: One agent run / conversation. Approvals and state are scoped to it.

call_id.description: Optional id of this tool call (the model's tool_call id). Recorded with the answer.

project_root.description: Project folder (default: cwd). Approvals are scoped to it.

user_messages.description: Every user turn of the session, oldest first (semgate keeps the first and the newest 19).

user_message.description: The latest user turn (default: the last of user_messages).

recent.description: Earlier tool calls of this session, oldest first (semgate keeps the last 20). Pass `output` (what the tool returned) so the injection scan can read it.

summary.description: The command, path or URL of that call (cut to 500 characters).

output.description: What the tool returned (cut to 6000 characters). Untrusted data.

result.description: Short outcome, e.g. 'exit 1: error: ...' (cut to 300 characters).

agent_intent.description: The agent's latest explanation of what it is doing. Untrusted: shown to the judge as the agent's claim only (cut to 2000 characters).

model.description: Model id of the agent (recorded as evidence only).

session_started_at.description: When the session started (ISO 8601 or epoch seconds); used by the history-rewrite signal.

timeout_ms.description: Deadline for this check. At the deadline the answer is ask.
